contract.headline: No authority layer is fully delayed — every measured layer contains at least one path with no established delay. Delays of 24h are measured on OTHER paths inside those same layers, and do not bound the undelayed ones.
contract.headline_basis: Derived from the layer rows below, not authored here, so it changes when the walk changes.

layers.terminal_name: Ethena TimelockController / Mint and Redeem V2 operators

paths.name: Ethena TimelockController
paths.hand_walk: Live owner() returned this TimelockController and pendingOwner() was zero. getMinDelay() returned 86400 seconds. The timelock itself holds DEFAULT_ADMIN; live hasRole checks show the same Dev Safe holds PROPOSER, EXECUTOR and CANCELLER, while the zero address holds none. The Safe is currently 5-of-10. Verified USDe source lets owner replace minter with any non-owner address; that replacement then has unrestricted token-level mint reach. TimelockController updateDelay is onlySelf, so reducing the delay must first clear the current 24h delay.

paths.name: Ethena Mint and Redeem V2
paths.hand_walk: Live minter() returned this direct, non-proxy contract. Its owner() and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE both resolve to the same 24h TimelockController. Current MINTER_ROLE operators can submit mint orders without that governance delay, but verified V2 logic constrains issuance by supported assets, signed orders, oracle tolerances and on-chain per-block limits; this path is therefore not represented as the full arbitrary token-level mint reach held by setMinter governance. The mutable operator set was not promoted to a fixed signer topology.

unresolved: ethereum contract-upgrade: measured absence, not an unresolved authority. USDe is direct bytecode, its EIP-1967 implementation/admin/beacon slots are zero, and verified source contains no upgrade mechanism. setMinter authority is represented under asset-permission.
